sections.label: Climate Action pledge sign-ups
sections.summary: About 50,000 individuals, organisations and educational institutions have taken the Climate Action pledge since its January launch.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since launching in January, about 50,000 individuals, organisations and educational institutions have taken the Climate Action pledge.

sections.label: World Bank climate-smart investment estimate
sections.summary: The World Bank estimates US$23 trillion in climate-smart investments is needed to meet the Paris commitments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The World Bank estimates that climate-smart investments amounting to US$23 trillion will be needed to meet the Paris commitments, that means, US$23 trillion in demand for clean energy, low-emissions transport and sustainable urban solutions.

sections.label: Carbon tax spending and energy efficiency
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said Singapore is prepared to spend more than it collects in carbon taxes over five years to help companies improve carbon efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has clearly stated that we are prepared to spend more than what we collect in carbon taxes over the next five years to help our companies, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs), improve their carbon efficiency and shift to the low-carbon economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our companies reported an energy efficiency (EE) improvement rate of 0.4% in 2014 and 0.6% in 2015.

sections.label: Taxable facilities emissions threshold
sections.summary: Taxable facilities are those emitting 25,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalent or more of GHG emissions annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Taxable facilities are those that emit 25,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalent (tCO2e) and above of GHG emissions annually.

sections.label: Threshold facilities share of emissions
sections.summary: Facilities crossing the threshold account for about 80% of Singapore's GHG emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Together, the facilities that cross this threshold account for about 80% of Singapore's GHG emissions.

sections.label: Reportable facilities measurement and reporting
sections.summary: Reportable facilities emitting at least 2,000 but less than 25,000 tonnes must measure and report GHG emissions but are not taxed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we still want to encourage smaller emitters to monitor and reduce their emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, the second category called "reportable facilities", that is, those that emit at least 2,000 tonnes but less than 25,000 tonnes, must have their GHG emissions measured and reported, but will not be taxed.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate and increase
sections.summary: The carbon tax starts at S$5 per tonne of GHG emissions and the Government intends to raise it to S$10 to S$15 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As announced by the Finance Minister in the 2018 Budget, the carbon tax rate will start at S$5 per tonne of GHG emissions, which the Government intends to raise to between S$10 to S$15 by 2030.

sections.label: Biofuel emissions and excise duties
sections.summary: GHG emissions not counted under international protocols, such as carbon dioxide from biofuels, will not get an additional carbon tax as excise duties already apply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The list also includes GHG emissions that, in line with international GHG reporting protocols, are not counted towards a company's emissions, such as the carbon dioxide emissions from biofuels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As highlighted by the Finance Minister in his recent Budget Statement, excise duties have been levied on these fuels, which already encourage reduction of their use and, therefore, reduce GHG emissions and, hence, no additional carbon tax will be levied.

sections.label: Penalties pegged to Income Tax Act
sections.summary: Penalties on taxable facilities for reporting and tax payment are pegged to equivalent Income Tax Act penalties for fraud and tax evasion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Given that we are imposing a tax on GHG emissions, for parity, the penalties on taxable facilities relating to reporting and tax payment have been pegged to the equivalent penalties for fraud and tax evasion in the Income Tax Act.

sections.label: Minister delegates appeal to Panel
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Minister to delegate an appeal to a Panel with at least one person having requisite technical expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, the Bill allows the Minister to delegate the appeal to a Panel that must comprise at least one person with the requisite technical expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It will provide a price signal to incentivise energy and carbon efficiency improvement across the economy and encourage investment in clean, sustainable solutions.

sections.label: Singapore companies' energy efficiency rates
sections.summary: NEA noted companies achieved energy efficiency improvement rates of 0.4% in 2014, 0.6% in 2015 and 0.8% in 2016, below leading countries.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: NEA noted that our companies achieved an EE improvement rate of only 0.4% in 2014 and 0.6% in 2015 and, as the Minister mentioned just now, 0.8% in 2016, compared to the 1%-2% per annum achieved in leading countries, such as Belgium and the Netherlands.

sections.label: Carbon tax impact on households
sections.summary: At S$5 per tonne, the carbon tax impact is about 1% of total electricity and gas expense, or S$0.30 to S$1.10 monthly for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the current carbon tax rate of S$5 per tonne, on average, the impact of the carbon tax is expected to be small, at about 1% on total electricity and gas expense, or about S$0.30 per month for an HDB 1-room flat to about S$1.10 per month for an HDB executive flat.

sections.label: First Southeast Asian carbon tax
sections.summary: Singapore is the first Southeast Asian country to implement such a tax, signalling to neighbours the significance it places on transparency in environmental issues.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the first country in Southeast Asia to implement such a tax, we send a crucial signal to our Southeast Asian neighbours the significance we place on transparency when it comes to environmental issues.

sections.label: Carbon tax burden on low-income families
sections.summary: The carbon tax impact on households is estimated at about 1%, but it may still be a heavy burden for low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although it is estimated that the impact of carbon tax on the household is only about 1%, however, for low-income families, it may still be a heavy burden.

sections.label: Carbon tax rebate for energy-saving bulbs
sections.summary: MEWR will help 1-room and 2-room households switch to energy-saving bulbs, and the speaker suggests giving companies carbon tax rebates for helping households change bulbs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) mentioned earlier that it will help the 1-room and 2-room households to switch to energy-saving bulbs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I feel that if we allow companies to receive carbon tax rebate if they help the households to change bulbs, we can then tap on the effort of the business community to help all the households to change to energy-saving bulbs.

sections.label: Bill and Paris Agreement commitment
sections.summary: Singapore's intended nationally determined contribution aims to reduce emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions peaking around 2030, and this Bill is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's first intended nationally determined contribution under the Paris Agreement states that we intend to reduce our emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and to stabilise our emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In starting the journey towards imposing a cost to carbon emissions in line with this commitment and in line with the long-term externalities that carbon creates, this Bill is a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Carbon pricing scheme similarities
sections.summary: Key similarities include paying for government-issued carbon credits rather than direct fuel taxation, taxing only firms and not households, and taxing facilities with 25,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some key similarities are using the device for paying for carbon units issued by the Government called "carbon credits" in our legislation rather than direct taxation on fuel sources, imposing this only on firms and excepting households and only taxing facilities with 25,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, many countries which practise CP set the price at around US$20 mark, though many countries running pilot schemes also price it much lower than that.

sections.label: Fund for green technologies
sections.summary: The Finance Minister is willing to invest more than the carbon tax revenue in low carbon technologies, and the speaker asks whether part of the funds could go to a fund or green infrastructure bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the Finance Minister said that he is willing to invest even more than the revenue generated by this carbon tax in low carbon technologies and practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider setting aside part of the funds from the carbon tax into a vehicle like a fund or even a green infrastructure bank offering low-interest loans that has a mission to fund the development, testing and deployment of green technologies in Singapore?

sections.label: Public data on large emitters
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will consider making individual large emitters' emissions data publicly available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, will the Government consider making data on individual large emitters' emissions publicly available?

sections.label: Releasing sector emissions data
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will release emissions data for clusters of firms in sectors like oil refining and chemicals, and supports the Bill and a 2030 emissions cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If there are concerns about commercial sensitivity if individual company data is released, will the Government consider releasing emissions data for clusters of firms in specific sectors, such as oil refining and the manufacturing of specific categories of chemicals?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such data would help the public to benchmark the carbon intensity of our economic activities against global norms.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also support this Bill and celebrate the Ministry's commitment to a cap on the quantity of emissions by 2030, taking into account population and economic growth at that point.

sections.label: Addressing corporate sector concerns
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry plans to allay corporate sector concerns and encourage corporations to play their part in meeting the 2030 pledge.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry plan to allay this concern that the corporate sector has, and how would they encourage corporations to play their part as we pledge to meet 2030?

sections.label: Role in international carbon market
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry and NEA, with MOF and MTI, envision for Singapore's role in the international carbon market.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What does the Ministry and NEA envision – of course, acting in concert with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) – to actually have us take a role in the international carbon market?

sections.label: Singapore's position for COP24
sections.summary: The passage asks Singapore's current position preparing for COP24, given its trade partners in EU member states and China.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that Singapore has taken a position in Paris preferring a uniform approach at that point.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But given that we have such huge trade partners in both the EU member states as well as China, what is our current position as we prepare for COP24?

sections.label: Sharing carbon tax results and mitigating costs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government to regularly share results of the carbon tax on residents' energy consumption and to consider mitigating cost of living for retirees and the sandwich class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, it would be helpful if, at regular intervals, the Government can share the results of the carbon tax on lowering the energy consumption of residents of Singapore, which should exclude the manufacturers' energy consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, I hope that the Government will consider mitigating the additional cost of living not just for the most vulnerable Singaporeans, which the Minister for Finance has announced, but also for our retirees and our sandwich class.

sections.label: Indirect compliance and administrative costs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can share the likely indirect compliance and administrative cost for carbon-emitting industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government share with us the likely indirect compliance and administrative cost that carbon-emitting industries will have to incur?

sections.label: Impact on industry competitiveness
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government to share how the measure will impact industry competitiveness, especially petrochemicals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fifth, I hope the Government can also share how it will impact the competitiveness of our industry, especially for, let us say, the petrochemicals industry.

sections.label: Derivation of carbon tax rate
sections.summary: The passage states the carbon tax rate is $5 per tonne of carbon dioxide in the Bill and asks how it was derived.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The carbon tax rate is $5 per tonne of carbon dioxide in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How is this tax rate derived and determined?

sections.label: Concerns on Fixed Price Credit Based system
sections.summary: The passage states green groups shared concerns on the Fixed Price Credit Based system, which seems to require companies to purchase credits at the start of each reporting period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Green groups have shared concerns on the implementation of the Fixed Price Credit Based (FPCB) system, as it seems to require companies to purchase credits at the beginning of each reporting period.

sections.label: Revenue funding green initiatives
sections.summary: The passage states the Ministry said tax revenue will fund green initiatives via the Productivity Grant (Energy Efficiency) and the Energy Efficiency Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry has said that revenue from the tax will fund the green initiatives via two existing schemes: the Productivity Grant (Energy Efficiency) (PG (EE)), and the Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F).

sections.label: Soft start and incremental approach
sections.summary: The passage states the Government chose a soft start and incremental approach, imposing a lower tax per tonne at the beginning and increasing it over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are clearly challenges in implementing such a bold and new initiative to regulate conduct and practices which have been in place for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is understandable and commendable, therefore, that the Government has chosen a soft start and an incremental approach by imposing a lower tax per tonne of emission at the beginning and increasing the same over time.

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue and spending
sections.summary: The Government expects about S$1 billion in carbon tax revenues over five years and is prepared to spend more than that on abatement projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government is expected to collect carbon tax revenues of about S$1 billion over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note that the Minister for Finance had indicated that the Government is prepared to spend more than the revenue generated from the carbon tax within the same period to support worthwhile projects which deliver the necessary abatement in emissions, and the Minister had earlier repeated this in his speech.

sections.label: Businesses blaming costs, profiteering
sections.summary: Some businesses attribute cost increases to water, GST and carbon tax before they are imposed, prompting a question on monitoring knock-on effects and regulating unfair profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some businesses have attributed the increases in cost to the cost of water as well as to the prospective increase in Goods and Services Tax (GST) and the carbon tax, even when they have yet to be imposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, wonder if there is any way for the Government to monitor the knock-on effect of the implementation of the carbon tax on consumers and put in place some regulation to avoid unfair profiteering.

sections.label: Monitoring profiteering and reducing carbon footprint
sections.summary: The speaker suggests monitoring to prevent unfair profiteering, urges people to reduce their carbon footprint, and calls for fair legislation and sustained education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government can try to monitor this and do something so that companies and businesses do not take the opportunity to engage in unfair profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I think that people should also be aware and change their way of life gradually and reduce our carbon footprint.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We can cut waste, reduce usage of electrical devices, we can walk more instead of taking the car, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We will save money and, at the same time, we save the environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am sure that with fair and balanced legislation, and sustained educational efforts, we can realise our vision of preserving a beautiful environment for our children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is important for us to do our part to protect the environment, but this needs to go beyond platitudes and be translated into actual action.

sections.label: Major emitters share of emissions
sections.summary: Greenhouse gas emissions from 30 major emitters account for 80% of total carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The GHG emission from these 30 major emitters accounts for 80% of our total carbon emission.

sections.label: Electricity cost rise and measurement questions
sections.summary: The Government estimates electricity costs will rise 30 cents monthly for a 1-room flat and $1.10 for an executive flat, and asks how measurement standards and tax levels are decided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has estimated that for a 1-room flat, electricity costs will increase by only 30 cents per month and for an executive flat, $1.10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): I would like to ask the Minister how the Ministry determines what standard of measurement of carbon emissions to use, and the types and quantities of classified substances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Going forward, how would the Ministry decide when to increase or decrease the minimum taxable quantums and the appropriate tax levels?

sections.label: Carbon tax rate and goals
sections.summary: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked whether the proposed carbon tax rate of S$5 per tonne of GHG emissions will affect the ability to meet goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked whether our proposed carbon tax rate of S$5 per tonne of GHG emissions will affect our ability to meet our goals.

sections.label: Carbon tax rate transition
sections.summary: Carbon tax starts at S$5 per tonne for five years, with review by 2023 and intended increase to S$10-S$15 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Whilst companies understood the need to price carbon, they asked for a transition period to adjust to the impact of the tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is why we are starting with S$5 per tonne for the first five years; companies will have time to adjust, for example, by upgrading to more energy-efficient equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In response to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, the Minister for Finance has said that we will, in fact, review the carbon tax rate by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We intend to increase the level to S$10 to S$15 per tonne of GHG emissions by 2030.

sections.label: Buying and surrendering credits
sections.summary: Companies can buy credits from NEA at a fixed price and must surrender credits equal to their preceding year's tax liability by 30 September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Companies can buy credits from NEA at a fixed price throughout the year but must surrender credits equivalent to their preceding year's tax liability by 30 September.

sections.label: Carbon tax impact on households
sections.summary: Carbon tax impact on households is expected to be about 1% of electricity and gas expenses, with eligible HDB households receiving S$20 yearly U-Save rebates from 2019 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Henry Kwek spoke about the impact of the carbon tax on households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is expected to be small, at about 1% of total electricity and gas expenses, on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As the Minister for Finance announced at Budget 2018, eligible HDB households will receive additional U-Save rebates of S$20 per year, from 2019 to 2021.

sections.label: Globalfoundries replacing high warming gas
sections.summary: With Government support, Globalfoundries is replacing a high global warming potential process chamber cleaning gas with one that has none, cutting emissions by over 400,000 tonnes when completed in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: With further support from the Government, Globalfoundries is working to replace a process chamber cleaning gas that has high global warming potential with one that has no global warming potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This will reduce their emissions significantly by more than 400,000 tonnes, when completed in 2019.

sections.label: Spending carbon tax revenue
sections.summary: The Government is prepared to spend more than the estimated S$1 billion in carbon tax revenue collected in the first five years on carbon abatement projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Government is prepared to spend more than the estimated S$1 billion in carbon tax revenue that will be collected in the first five years, on worthwhile carbon abatement projects.

sections.label: Solar forecasting research grant
sections.summary: Last October, EMA awarded a S$6.2 million research grant to develop solar forecasting capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Last October, EMA also awarded a S$6.2 million research grant to develop our solar forecasting capabilities.

sections.label: Shell co-generation and renewables spending
sections.summary: The speaker opened Singapore's third co-generation plant, which improved refinery energy efficiency and cut carbon emissions, while Shell plans increased new energies spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In Singapore, I officiated the opening of their third co-generation plant which improved the refinery’s EE by 4% to 5% and reduces their carbon emissions by 265,000 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Similarly, Shell has been reaching into the next energy frontier with renewables and hydrogen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: They intend to increase their spending in their new energies business arm to about US$1 billion to US$2 billion per year until 2020.

sections.label: Singapore advocated NDC concept
sections.summary: Singapore advocated the NDC concept and worked with like-minded countries to get it adopted by UNFCCC under the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Singapore was the advocate for the very concept of the NDC and worked with other like-minded countries to get it adopted by UNFCCC under the Paris Agreement.
